PullRequest.Title: sessions: show the active chat as the session view by default
PullRequest.Body:

`sessions.showChatTabs` now defaults to `single`: the Agents window shows a session's active chat as the session view instead of a tab per chat.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9807

## Change

- `SESSIONS_CHAT_TABS_DEFAULT` is now `single`. The setting's registration, the session view, and the accessibility help all read it.
- The setting keeps `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`, and explicit user settings still win.
- **Show Chat Tabs** in the session's overflow menu still switches between **Single** and **Multiple**.
- Tests: the registration test now pins `single` as the default, and the accessibility help test's default case expects the single-chat description.

## How to test

1. Run this branch from sources, so no experiment assignment applies, and open the Agents window without `sessions.showChatTabs` in your user settings.
2. Open a session that has more than one chat. The active chat fills the session view, without a tab row.
3. In the session's overflow menu, open **Show Chat Tabs**: **Single** is checked. Choose **Multiple**, and the chats show as tabs again.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/sessions/**/*.test.js'`: passed, 10488 passing, 27 pending. Before the accessibility help test was updated, its default case failed, as expected.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npx eslint` on the three changed files: passed.
- Not tested manually in a running Agents window.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an existing multi-chat session with no explicit sessions.showChatTabs setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration resolution selects Single, then ChatGroupsView restores/creates the grid and ChatGroupView creates one active ChatView. The active transcript load remains on the existing session-opening critical path; the diff adds no awaited work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and JSON-parse the workspace-stored per-session chat-group layouts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage read per session view setup; serialized content scales with previously persisted split groups, not with the new default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Multiple mode used the same storage read and restore path with the same call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous setup work before the grid can be restored.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the active chat view and load/render its transcript through the existing ChatView.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active ChatView for the normal single-group session in both modes; additional views only correspond to explicitly restored split groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Multiple mode also created one ChatGroupView and one active ChatView; it additionally rendered the tab strip and assigned all visible chats to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The active view must exist before the session transcript is rendered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible chats and persisted split groups. In the common unsplit case, Single assigns only the active chat to the sole group and suppresses tab DOM, while Multiple assigned all visible chats to the tab bar.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grid/group construction is synchronous and sequential; transcript loading behavior is unchanged and remains owned by the active ChatView.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Loaded session/chat models and transcript state are reused as before. Persisted layout lookup has identical cold/warm behavior; changing the default neither adds a cache key nor defeats coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constant reaches ChatGroupsView directly, and both branches were traced through group creation, reconciliation, and ChatView creation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transcript size and provider latency vary, but the changed literal does not increase view count, transcript loads, or storage calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The default Single path creates the same one expensive active chat view and less tab DOM/work for an unsplit session.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch from one chat to another in the same session under the new Single default
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit navigation resolves the session/chat, waits for any existing provider-backed session load, updates the active chat, then reuses the current ChatView via setChat and reloads the selected transcript. This is the same openChat path used before when selecting a tab.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider-backed session/chat state and wait for the session to load; provider implementations may cross the extension-host or remote boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolution/load sequence per explicit chat navigation, cancellation-coalesced by the existing navigation token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selecting a chat tab in Multiple mode invoked the same SessionsService.openChat path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested chat cannot display until provider-backed state is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clear the previous transcript state and load/render the newly selected chat in the retained widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transcript switch per explicit chat navigation; no per-visible-chat fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Multiple mode reused the same active ChatView and called setChat when switching tabs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to render the selected chat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User chat-navigation frequency and selected transcript size; the total number of hidden chats does not cause transcript loads in Single mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Navigation uses existing cancellation so superseded opens do not produce an unbounded concurrent burst; rendering remains one active chat per group.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same chat model/view-state and transcript reuse paths apply in both modes; the default does not change positive, negative, or in-flight cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the mode-specific reconciliation changes only group assignment/presentation; navigation and transcript-loading implementations are shared.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and transcript latency vary, but call cardinality and cancellation are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Switching presentation does not add provider calls or recreate the ChatView.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or explicitly open side-by-side chat groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Persisted groups are deserialized and one ChatGroupView/ChatView is created per restored pane, or a new group is created on an explicit open-to-side action; grid layout then runs for those groups.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize all split groups and store the workspace layout after topology or active-group changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full layout write per existing persistence trigger; payload scales with explicit split-group count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same split layout serialization and storage triggers applied under Multiple mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous persistence occurs after reconciliation/layout actions, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicitly created or restored split groups, not total chats. Each group owns one expensive chat widget in both modes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Group creation and grid layout are synchronous/sequential; explicit chat opens use the existing single navigation flow.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted layouts are keyed by session ID and reused identically in both modes. The default does not create additional persisted groups automatically.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reconciliation replaces an unpinned peer in place under Single mode; new groups require pinning, restoration, drag/drop, or explicit open-to-side actions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can create varying numbers of panes, but Single mode does not automatically fan chats out into groups.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression caused by the default change. Any multi-widget cost is tied to explicit/restored split panes and existed before.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessibility help performs one configuration lookup and appends the mode-specific localized strings; no asynchronous or external work is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work independent of session/chat count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration lookup behavior is unchanged; only the fallback enum value differs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only runtime consumer in this path branches between predeclared localized text.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; tests only update the expected fallback wording.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced the changed default through configuration registration, ChatGroupsView reconciliation, ChatGroupView/ChatView lifecycle, session navigation, layout persistence, and accessibility help. The new Single default does not add boundary calls, eager views, repeated transcript work, or concurrency; for the common unsplit case it suppresses tab rendering and assigns only the active chat.
